Vanessa —

We reviewed the renewal numbers internally and we have a mid-term ask: our analytics team will need an additional 25% capacity starting Dec 1 to support a pilot. We'd like to roll that into the renewal rather than sign a separate short-term addendum. The current renewal is coterming to 12/31/2026; can you confirm what the pro-rata for the extra capacity would look like and whether we can get any pricing relief given the expansion?

Also procurement asked whether a single amendment can both: (1) add capacity and (2) align the contract to calendar year (co-term). If so, what does the credit/charge calculation look like?

Claire —

Thanks for the heads up and the Q3 usage file, that helps. Short answer: yes, we can bundle the mid-term capacity add into the renewal amendment and co-term to 12/31/2026. I want to make sure we align on three items before I send an official amendment:

1) Sizing: confirm the target additional committed throughput (you mentioned ~25% — can you confirm as tokens/day or reserved GPU hours?).
2) Pricing treatment: we typically bill the remainder of the current term pro-rata for the added capacity, then normalize to the annualized rate at co-term. For customers adding mid-contract, we offer a one-time onboarding credit in lieu of a lower list discount — I can propose that.
3) Timing & DocuSign: need procurement sign-off for the amendment and a DocuSign link.

I looped in Rafael (sales leadership) for approval on the onboarding credit and Marissa from RevOps for the pro-rata math and contract language. If you can confirm the sizing by tomorrow, I’ll follow up with a revised quote and a proposed amendment document.

Best,

Vanessa / Marissa —

Thanks for the loop. I’m ok with bundling the mid-term add into the amendment, provided we keep the uplift conservative. Proposal framework:

- Additional capacity = +25% of committed Q3 baseline (per Claire). Suggest translating to reserved hours: +600 reserved GPU hours/month.
- Pricing: apply a one-time onboarding credit equal to 10% of the pro-rata charge for the remainder of the current term, then annualize the added capacity at a 6% discount to list for the new co-term rate.
- If they push for a flat percentage discount on the whole renewal instead, escalate to me (but prefer the credit + modest uplift route).

Marissa — can you run the pro-rata calc and produce the amendment language snippets for a 12/31 co-term (include sample DocuSign clause for immediate effect on Dec 1)? I’ll standby for approval.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-11-05T14:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation and mid-term request

Hi all —

I ran the numbers using the usage file Claire sent. Summary:

- Baseline committed: 2,400 reserved GPU hours/month. Q3 average usage suggests baseline is on target.
- Requested add: +25% => +600 reserved GPU hours/month.
- Pro-rata for remainder of current term (Nov 15–Dec 31, 46 days): pro-rata charge for added capacity = (600 hours/month) * (list unit $4.00/hr) * (46/30) = $11,040 list.
- Onboarding credit (10% of pro-rata): $1,104 credit applied to the Dec invoice.
- New annualized co-term rate (effective 01/01/2027): added capacity annualized at 6% discount vs list => unit $3.76/hr. Annualized cost for the added capacity = 600 * 24 * 365 * $3.76/hr (we provide the calc line in the amendment).

I’ve drafted amendment language (short form) and included a sample DocuSign clause that: (A) amends the SOW to add 600 hours/month effective 12/1/2026; (B) applies the onboarding credit to the Dec invoice; and (C) sets the new co-term to 12/31/2027 with the annualized pricing above.

Next steps: Vanessa — confirm Claire is comfortable with the credit + 6% discount structure. Claire — if procurement needs a different way to show the discount (flat % off renewal vs credit), say so and we’ll run that variant.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Revenue Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
